raw_response:
I still do the wheat-maize on all 9.8 mu, same as my land has done these years. I do not dare change much. Our house is small, and some people go out for work, so I cannot make things too complicated or spend too much cash at one time. Wheat cannot be too thin, otherwise I worry about poor ears. Maize after wheat must be planted fast, so I keep the turnaround simple: harvest wheat, clear the field, shallow till or rotary once if I can get the machine, then sow maize right away. I use the well when the crop really needs it, but pumping costs money, so I will not water too many times unless the season turns dry.

For wheat, I will use the usual seed from the dealer, not the expensive fancy kind. I put a base fertilizer before sowing, then one more urea topdressing around jointing if the leaves look weak or yellow. Wheat usually needs more water here, so I plan a few irrigations: one after sowing if the soil is dry, one at jointing, one at grain filling if there is no rain. For maize, I keep it plain and fast because the wheat harvest and maize planting are very close together. I buy hybrid maize seed, put fertilizer once at planting and once when it grows taller, and usually water once or twice depending on rain. I only spray pesticide if I really see weeds or insects. I want steady grain, not the highest yield on paper.
